Species richness and diversity per site and occasion

Source: R/07_richness.R
pam_richness.Rd

Turns the cleaned detections into species richness and diversity: for every site and time bin, for every site over the whole survey, and across sites (species accumulation and an estimate of how many species were missed). The site table can be joined to habitat covariates by site_id to study how richness varies with the environment.

Usage

pam_richness(
  cfg,
  run_id = cfg$birdnet$run_id,
  bin_days = NULL,
  min_events = 1,
  abundance = c("counts", "presence"),
  q = c(1, 2),
  thresholds = NULL,
  species = NULL,
  min_effort_hours = NULL,
  write = FALSE
)

Arguments

cfg

A pam_config object.

run_id

Detection run (sub-folder of paths$detections).

bin_days

Length of a time bin in days. NULL uses occupancy$occasion_length_days (1 if not set).

min_events

A species counts as present in a site and bin only when it has at least this many events there (a whole number, default 1). A higher number removes species known only from a lone, possibly false, detection, at the cost of missing rare species.

abundance

How species are weighted in the Hill numbers: "counts" (the default; the number of events, an activity-based measure) or "presence" (every present species weighs the same, so only occurrence matters).

q

Orders of the Hill numbers to compute besides richness (default 1 and 2). Richness is the Hill number of order 0 and is always returned.

thresholds

Optional per-species thresholds (a data frame, or the path of a CSV file, with scientific_name and threshold), for example from pam_species_thresholds().

species

Optional species to keep (scientific names, common names or species labels). NULL keeps all.

min_effort_hours

Minimum recorded hours for a bin to count as surveyed. NULL uses occupancy$min_effort_hours (2 if not set).

write

If TRUE, also save the four tables to <outputs>/<run_id>/ as richness_occasions.csv, richness_sites.csv, species_accumulation.csv and richness_estimates.csv.

Value

A list of class pam_richness:

  • occasions: one row per site and bin: richness, hill_q<q> columns, n_events (events of the species counted as present), effort_hours, n_days, sufficient. Bins below the minimum effort are kept and flagged.

  • sites: one row per site, using only surveyed bins: richness, hill_q<q>, n_events, n_occasions_surveyed, effort_hours.

  • accumulation: the expected number of species (richness) for n_sites = 1 to the number of surveyed sites.

  • estimates: one row with the observed richness, the Chao2 estimate of the total and completeness (observed divided by estimated).

  • settings: the choices that were used.

Details

Hill numbers

Hill numbers describe diversity as an effective number of species. Order 1 is the number of equally common species that gives the same Shannon diversity, and order 2 the same for the Simpson index; larger orders give more weight to the dominant species. With abundance = "counts" a loud, vocal species weighs more than a quiet one, so the numbers describe the acoustic community; use "presence" when only occurrence matters. A bin with no species has richness 0 and NA for the other orders.

Accumulation and the estimate

Sites are the sampling units. accumulation is the exact expected number of species found in n randomly chosen surveyed sites (sample-based rarefaction), so curves from different projects can be compared at the same number of sites. The Chao2 estimate uses how many species were found in only one or two sites to estimate how many remain undetected; treat it as a lower bound. A species with a false-positive detection counts as present, so validated thresholds and min_events matter for all of these numbers.

See also

pam_plot_richness(), pam_detection_table()

Examples

ex <- pam_example_project()
# the later stages read the master table that the scan builds
res <- suppressMessages(pam_scan_audio(ex$cfg))
proc <- suppressMessages(pam_process_detections(ex$cfg))
rich <- suppressMessages(pam_richness(ex$cfg))
as.data.frame(rich$sites)[, c("site_id", "richness", "hill_q1", "hill_q2")]
#>   site_id richness  hill_q1  hill_q2
#> 1   G0059        2 1.960132 1.923077
#> 2   G0110        3 2.871746 2.777778
rich$estimates
#>    n_sites observed singletons doubletons chao2 completeness
#>      <int>    <int>      <int>      <int> <num>        <num>
#> 1:       2        3          1          2 3.125         0.96
# count a species only when it has at least two events in a bin
strict <- suppressMessages(pam_richness(ex$cfg, min_events = 2))
strict$sites$richness
#> [1] 2 2
